runBy: owner, Neon SQL console, read-only; aggregate counts only; Claude had no production access
sql: SELECT count(*) AS apple_links, count(*) FILTER (WHERE u.password_hash IS NULL) AS apple_without_password, count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM native_auth_providers g WHERE g.user_id = u.id AND g.provider_type = 'google')) AS apple_with_google FROM native_auth_providers p JOIN native_users u ON u.id = p.user_id WHERE p.provider_type = 'apple';

conclusions.upperBound: One account could have the R3-10 shape: an Apple link, no password, and Google linked as well. Whether its Apple link was made from an unverified address cannot be read from the data; the account has to be identified.
conclusions.decision5: Decision 5 closes R3-10 once the owner confirms that the Apple and the Google sign-in on that one account belong to the same person. If not, that account is handled on its own.
conclusions.alternative: Extending the rule to other links would reach exactly this account: its Apple link would be removed at the next Google proof.
